audio.t: Hello, everyone. My name is Dina and I'm going to tell you about our school's podcast, which we started last autumn.
At first, the idea came from our music teacher. He wanted students to share their ideas, not only to listen to adults. I thought it sounded too difficult, but now it is my favorite activity.
We publish a new show every Thursday, and each one lasts about ten minutes. A short show is better because people listen to it on the way home.
You don't need expensive equipment. We use a phone and a thick blanket. If we record under the blanket, the sound is much clearer because there is no echo.
The hardest part is not talking. It's cutting the recording, because we always have too much, and we hate to delete anything.

If you like listening, you can help us. Send us a question about school life through the website and we'll answer it in the next show. We'd also like some students to write short stories for us to read.
Next term we plan to invite a visitor to each show, maybe a local baker or a football coach. So please come and join us.

audio.t: Today I'm talking to Sofia, who is fifteen and makes short videos about drawing. Sofia, how did you start?
Well, I was drawing in my notebook during a long train journey and my cousin filmed it. She said it looked cool, so I put it online. I never thought anybody would watch.
How many people watch your videos now?
About two thousand. That's small for some people, but it's more than the number of students in my school, so I'm very happy.
Do you spend a lot of time on it?
Only at weekends. During the week I have homework and basketball practice. If I did it every day, I would stop enjoying it.
Have you ever received unkind comments?
A few times. At first I was upset and I didn't draw for a week. Now I just delete them and block the person. My mum also taught me to talk to someone when I feel bad.
What advice would you give to a teenager who wants to start a channel?
Don't copy other people. Show your own ideas, even if they seem strange. And never share your address or school name online.
And what's next for you?
I'd like to give a drawing class for younger children online, but my parents say I must wait until I'm sixteen. I think that's reasonable.

items.text:
My week without social media

Last month my older brother said that I looked at my phone more than at the people around me. I laughed at first, but then I counted the hours on my screen. It was nearly five hours a day! So I decided to stop using social media for one week and write about it.

The first two days were the hardest. Every time I felt bored, my hand went to my pocket, even though I had deleted the apps. I also felt left out. My friends were talking about a funny video, and I had no idea what it was. At lunch I almost said, 'Just show me!' but I kept my promise.

On the third day, something changed. I had finished my homework by six o'clock, which never happens, so I went for a walk with my dog. In the evening I read half a book and played cards with my parents. We laughed a lot, and my dad told us funny stories about his school days. I realized I hadn't heard those stories before because I was always busy with my phone.

Of course, it wasn't perfect. I missed some news from my football team, and my friend Nora was a bit angry because I did not answer her messages for two days. I explained what I was doing, and she understood. She even said she would like to try the same thing.

After seven days I was happy to go back, but I do it differently now. I check my phone only after homework, and I keep it in the kitchen at night. I don't think social media is bad. It helps me to stay in touch with my cousins in Canada. But I learned that I am the one who decides how much time it takes. If you are not sure how you feel about your own phone, try it for just three days. You may be surprised.

items.q: Why did the writer decide to stop using social media?
options: She wanted to know if she could live without it.
items.vi: Sau lời nhận xét của anh trai và khi thấy gần 5 giờ mỗi ngày, cô muốn thử sống không có mạng xã hội.

items.q:
You see this announcement in an English-language magazine for teenagers.

ARTICLES WANTED: Is social media good or bad for teenagers?
Tell us what you think. Write about the good things, the bad things and your own experience.

Write your article (about 100 words).
items.sample: Social media is a big part of my life, and I think it has both good and bad sides. First, it helps me to keep in touch with friends and family who live far away. I can also learn new things, for example how to draw or how to cook, by watching short videos. However, there are some problems. Many teenagers spend too much time online and sleep too little. Some people also write unkind comments, and this can make others feel sad. In my experience, the best way is to set a time limit. I use my phone for one hour after homework, and then I go outside or talk to my family. In conclusion, social media is useful if we use it carefully.

items.text:
When our school canteen began using plastic cups and spoons a year ago, I counted how many we threw away in one day. I stopped at four hundred. I was shocked, and that night I could not stop thinking about it. The next morning I asked my teacher, Mr. Okafor, if I could start a recycling club.

At first, only three people came: me, my best friend Lina and a boy called Theo, who just wanted to be somewhere warm at lunchtime. We made posters, but nobody read them. We put colored bins in the corridors, but students still threw everything into the same one. Honestly, I almost gave up. I thought people did not care.

Then Mr. Okafor gave me some advice. He said that people do not change because they are told to. They change when something is easy and when it is fun. So we tried a new idea and turned recycling into a competition between classes. Every Friday we weighed the paper and plastic that each class had collected, and the winners got a plant for their classroom.

Suddenly everybody was interested. Students carried bottles from home, and Class 8C even asked the teachers to bring their old newspapers. Within two months the club grew from three members to thirty-five, and the school threw away almost half as much rubbish as before.

The best surprise came last week. The canteen manager told us that he was going to buy paper cups and metal spoons instead of plastic ones. He said our club had shown him how much waste the school made. I felt so proud that I did not know what to say.

I have learned that one small idea can grow if you do not give up. I am not saying that a club can save the planet. But I do believe that if every school tried something similar, it would make a real difference. And you do not need to be a scientist to begin. You just need to count your rubbish, like I did.

audio.t: Welcome to Teen Health Hour. Today Dr. Carla Reyes is here to talk about sleep.
Thank you. Many teenagers need about nine hours of sleep each night, but most only get six or seven.
The main problem is screens. Looking at a phone in bed keeps your brain awake, so I suggest turning it off an hour before bed.
Another tip is to keep the same bedtime every day, even on weekends. A lot of students sleep until noon on Sunday, and then they can't sleep that night.
Food matters too. A big dinner late at night can make sleep difficult, and so can sweet drinks. A glass of warm milk is a better choice.
Finally, exercise. A walk or a bike ride after school helps you fall asleep faster, but don't do hard exercise just before bed.
Thank you, Dr. Reyes. That's all we have time for.

audio.t: Today I'm talking to Jake Morrison, who is sixteen and trains for long-distance races. Jake, when did you start running?
When I was twelve. I was not good at team sports, and my uncle said running was a way to get fit without a team.
How often do you train now?
Five days a week, usually before school at six o'clock. On Wednesdays I rest, and on Sundays I go for a long run with friends.
That's early! Is it hard to get up?
At first it was. Now I go to bed at nine thirty, so I wake up feeling fine.
What do you eat before a race?
Pasta, usually, with some vegetables. I never eat chocolate or fast food the day before, because it makes me slow.
Have you ever been hurt?
Last year I hurt my knee because I bought cheap shoes. The doctor told me to rest for a month. Now I always buy proper running shoes.
What advice do you have for other teenagers?
Start slowly and do something you enjoy. You don't have to run. You can dance or swim. The important thing is to move every day.

items.text:
Last January, I made a promise to myself. I was fifteen, and I spent most of my free time on the sofa with my phone. My mother said I looked pale, and my doctor agreed that I should move more. I did not want to join a gym or a sports team, because I thought everybody there would be better than me. So I decided to start small.

First, I walked to school instead of taking the bus. It took thirty minutes, and on the first morning my legs were sore and I was in a bad mood. But after a week I noticed something strange: I felt more awake in my first lesson, and I could think more clearly. My friend Ellie started walking with me, and our conversations made the time pass quickly.

In March, we found a free dance video online and practiced in my living room every Tuesday and Thursday. We laughed a lot, mostly at ourselves. I was terrible at it, but nobody was watching, so I did not mind. By summer, I could do a whole dance without stopping.

The biggest change, however, was my sleep. I used to lie awake until midnight. Now I am tired by ten, and I sleep deeply. My grades have even improved a little, although I am not sure the two things are connected.

I am not saying that everyone should do what I did. Some people prefer swimming, and others love team games. My point is simple: you do not need expensive equipment or a perfect body to begin. You only need to choose something that feels fun, and do it regularly. If you wait until you feel ready, you may wait forever.

If you do not like water, you could try cycling or badminton. To stay healthy, I play basketball twice a week and I walk to school every day. I also try to eat fruit and vegetables and to drink a lot of water. Another important thing is sleep. I go to bed at ten o'clock, so I always feel fresh in the morning. audio.t: Hello, listeners, and welcome to Teen Screen. Today I want to tell you about the Maple Hill Film Club, which started two years ago with only six members.
Now it has forty members, so they have moved from the small art room to the school theater. The club meets every Thursday afternoon at four o'clock.
Each week, the members watch a short film and talk about it. Last month they watched an old silent film with live piano music, and many students said it was their favorite evening.

In the spring, the club will make its own film. A teacher, Mr. Reed, will help with the camera, but the students will write the story themselves. The film will be about a lost dog that finds its way home.

If you want to join, you do not need to pay. You only need to bring a notebook, because everyone writes a short review after each film. The next meeting is a special one. Instead of a film, a real actor will visit the club and answer questions.

audio.t: Today my guest is Lena Park, who wrote her first novel when she was fifteen. Welcome, Lena.
Thank you. It is great to be here.
Your book, The Glass Garden, is about a girl who finds a garden inside a mirror. Where did the idea come from?
I saw an old mirror in my grandmother's attic. I imagined what could be on the other side, and I started writing that night.
How long did it take you to finish the book?
About eighteen months. I wrote mostly at weekends, because during the week I had school and piano lessons.
Was it hard to find a publisher?
Very hard. Five companies said no. My English teacher told me not to give up, and the sixth company said yes.
What do you do when you cannot think of a good sentence?
I go for a walk, or I read a few pages of someone else's book. Sitting and staring at the screen never works for me.
What advice would you give to young writers?
Read a lot, and write every day, even if it is only for ten minutes. And at first, show your work to just one friend you trust.

items.text:
My cousin Tara and I have argued about books and films for years. Last month we had our biggest argument yet, after we both watched the film of a famous adventure story. Tara loved it. I did not.

Tara says films are better because they are quicker. In two hours you know the whole story, and you can see the mountains, the ships and the strange animals, so you do not have to imagine them. She also says that you can watch a film with your friends and talk about it afterward, while reading is something you do alone.

I understand her point, but I do not agree. When I read a book, the pictures in my head are mine. The hero in my head has a face that nobody else has ever seen. In the film, the hero looked like a famous actor, and I could not forget that. Also, a film has to cut many parts of the story. My favorite scene in the book, where the hero talks to an old sailor in the rain, was not in the film at all. I was quite disappointed.

However, I have to be honest. Before the film, I had not touched that book for two years. After the film, I took it from the shelf and read it again in two days. So perhaps the film did something good. Tara also started reading the book last week, and she told me that it is "a different, bigger story". That made me smile.

In the end, we agreed on one idea. The best thing is to do both, but in the right order. I think you should read the book first, because then the film is a bonus. Tara thinks you should see the film first, because then the book gives you more. We still do not agree, but now we argue while we share our favorite books, and that is much more fun than before.

options: To explain how films are made.
To tell people to stop watching films.
To describe a disagreement about books and films.
items.vi: Bài viết kể về cuộc tranh cãi giữa tác giả và chị họ Tara về sách và phim.

items.sample: Hi Chris, thanks for your email. A film night sounds like a great idea! My favorite kind of film is comedy, because I love to laugh with my friends after a long day at school. I also enjoy adventure films, but I do not like scary ones. I would like to recommend a film about a funny robot who learns to play the drums. I think it is a good choice because it is exciting, and both younger and older students can enjoy it. I prefer going to the cinema, because the screen is huge and the sound is amazing. At home it is cheaper, but I often look at my phone and miss parts of the story. Please write soon and tell me which film you choose. Best wishes, Lan

items.q: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story for the school magazine. Your story must begin with this sentence: The music started and everyone turned to look. Write your story. Write 100 words or more.
items.sample: The music started and everyone turned to look. A small girl in a blue dress was standing alone on the stage with an old violin. Her name was Mina, and she had practiced for months for the school show. At first her hands shook, and the first notes were quiet and a little wrong. Then she saw her grandfather in the second row. He smiled and gave her a thumbs up. Mina closed her eyes and played the song he had taught her. The whole room became silent. When she finished, everybody stood up and clapped for a long time. Mina smiled happily, because she knew that she was not afraid of the stage anymore.
items.vi: Viết truyện bắt đầu bằng câu cho sẵn: dùng thì quá khứ, kể diễn biến (lúc đầu - sau đó - kết thúc) và cảm xúc của nhân vật.

audio.t: Today I'm talking to Kiara, a sixteen-year-old student from Brazil who is spending a year at a school in Scotland. Kiara, why did you decide to study abroad?
Well, my parents live in Brazil, not Canada! I wanted to improve my English, and I thought the best way was to live in an English-speaking place. It wasn't because I was bored. I was happy at home.
What surprised you most when you arrived?
The houses were normal, and lunch is at about twelve, like at home. But here, people shake hands when they meet. In Brazil we usually kiss on the cheek, so I felt a bit strange at first.
Was it hard to make friends?
Not really, everyone was kind. What was difficult was understanding fast speech. People talked so quickly that I only caught half of the words. Now it's much better.
How do you stay in touch with your family?
I don't write letters, and I don't send photos every day. But every Sunday we have a video call, and they tell me about everything at home.
And what do you miss most?
The weather is cold here, but I don't mind that. I like my new school, too. What I miss most is my little brother. He's only six, and he makes me laugh.
Finally, what advice would you give to other students?
Join a club and talk to everyone you can. Don't stay only with students from your own country, because then you won't learn so much. And you don't need to bring many books!

items.text:
A Year in Another Country

When I was fifteen, my parents agreed that I could spend a year at a school in Norway. I was very excited, but also a bit scared. I had never been away from home for more than a week, and I could not speak a word of Norwegian.

My host family lived in a small town near the sea. Their house was warm and quiet, and my host sister, Ingrid, was the same age as me. On the first evening, she showed me her favourite photos and tried to teach me a few words. I got most of them wrong, and we both laughed. That helped me relax.

School was very different from mine. Students called the teachers by their first names, and nobody wore a uniform. At first, I thought this was strange, and I wondered if lessons would be too easy. But the teachers expected us to think for ourselves, and the projects were much harder than I expected. I often had to ask Ingrid for help.

The hardest part of the year was the dark winter. In December, the sun came up at ten o'clock and went down at three. I felt tired and a little sad, and I missed my friends at home. Then Ingrid's mother gave me some good advice. She said that the best way to enjoy winter was to go outside, even when it was cold. So we went for long walks, and I started to notice the beautiful colours of the sky.

By spring, I could talk to people in the shops and understand the news on the radio. When it was time to go home, I cried at the airport. I had expected to come home with better language skills, and I did. But the biggest change was in me. I was now more patient and more confident, and I was not afraid of meeting new people. I am planning to visit Ingrid again next summer, and this time she will come with me to see my country.

audio.t: Today my guest is Noah Brandt. He is fourteen and he has made a reading lamp that switches on when a book is opened. Noah, how did you get the idea?
My little sister reads under her blanket at night with a flashlight, and the batteries were always empty. I thought, why not make a lamp that only works when she needs it?
How long did it take you?
About four months. I thought it would take two weeks, but my first designs did not work.
Where did you find the parts?
Most of them came from an old radio that my neighbor was throwing away. I only bought the small light, and it cost three dollars.
What was the hardest part?
The wires. I connected them in the wrong way, and the lamp turned on when the book was closed. That was funny, but my sister did not laugh.
What are you going to do next?
My teacher wants me to make five lamps for the school library. I will need help, so I am asking friends from my class.
What advice do you have for young inventors?
Do not wait for a big idea. Start with a small problem in your own house, and do not be afraid to ask questions.

items.text:
Three science clubs at Westbrook Community Center

A. Robot Builders
Mondays and Wednesdays, 4:30 to 6 p.m. For ages 11 to 15. Beginners are welcome, and laptops are provided. You learn to write programs for small robots, and in June every team takes part in a big robot contest. It costs $15 a month.

B. Star Gazers
Saturday evenings at 8 p.m. on the roof of the center. We have telescopes for everyone, and the club is free. Please wear warm clothes. If the sky is cloudy, the meeting is cancelled and we watch a short film about space instead.

C. Kitchen Chemistry
Tuesdays at 4 p.m. Try safe experiments with food, such as making your own ice cream and growing sugar crystals. Aprons are provided. It costs $5 a class. There are only eight places, so you must book a week before. Parents can stay and watch.

items.text:
The cane that talks to my grandfather

When I was thirteen, my grandfather Oskar started to lose his sight. He did not complain, but I noticed that he stopped going for walks because he was afraid of falling. I wanted to help, so I decided to make something for him.

My first idea was a cane with a small light, but my science teacher, Mr. Hollis, said that a light would not help a person who cannot see it. He suggested sound instead. That was a good idea, and I spent the next two months learning how a sensor can measure distance. I borrowed a book from the library and watched many videos, but most of them were too difficult, so I often asked Mr. Hollis for help after school.

The first version was a disaster. The sensor was fixed to a wooden stick with tape, and it beeped all the time, even when nothing was in front of it. My grandfather tried it in the garden and laughed so much that he nearly dropped it. I was upset, but he told me that every inventor makes silly mistakes before an idea works. I think those words are the reason I did not give up.

In the second version I changed the program so that the cane makes a quiet sound only when something is less than two meters away. The closer the object is, the faster the sound becomes. I also used a lighter plastic tube, which made the cane much easier to carry. After three more weeks of testing, my grandfather walked to the end of our street alone for the first time in a year. I stood at the corner and tried not to cry.

Last month I showed the cane at a regional science fair. I did not win a prize, but a woman from a company asked me for my email address. She said that many older people might want a similar tool at a low price. I do not know if anything will happen, but I am already working on a third version with a battery that lasts a week. For me, the best part of inventing is not the prize. It is seeing somebody use your idea in real life.

items.sample: Hi Chris, thanks for your email. A science fair sounds great! I think you should make a small alarm for your bedroom door. It is a simple invention, and it is useful because your little brother will not come in without asking. You need some wires, a small battery, a buzzer and a switch. items.text:
My grandfather, Walter, worked in the same bread factory for forty-two years. When he retired, the company gave him a watch and a big cake, and he cried a little. "It was a good life," he told me. "I always knew where I would be on Monday morning." I understand why that made him happy, but I do not think it is the life for me.

My mother is very different. She started as a hairdresser, then worked in a hotel, and now she teaches music to small children. Some of her friends thought she was making a mistake each time she changed. She says it was the best thing she ever did. "Each job taught me something new," she says, "and I never got bored." She also says it was frightening at first, especially the day she left the hotel without having another job to go to.

I am fifteen, and my teachers are already asking me what I want to be. I find this question quite hard. Last year I wanted to be a pilot. This year I think I would like to be a journalist. I have also thought about being a chef, and a teacher like my mother. My father says I should choose one and stop dreaming. He believes that students who decide early work harder at school. Perhaps he is right, but I think young people need time to find out what they enjoy.

Last month my school arranged a week of work experience, and I spent it in a local newspaper office. I expected it to be exciting, and some of it was. But I also found out that journalists spend a lot of time sitting at desks, checking facts and waiting for phone calls. That was not what I had imagined. A week earlier I might have said "journalist" without thinking, and I would have been wrong.

So my advice to other teenagers is simple. Do not worry if you do not have a plan yet. Try different things, ask adults about their work, and notice which days you enjoy most. A job is something you will do for many years, so it is worth taking your time. And if you change your mind later, like my mother, that is fine too.

options: His life was happy because it was predictable.

He was sad when he left the factory.

Read this email from your English friend Sam and the notes you have made.

Hi, I am thinking of getting a part-time job this summer. What kind of job do you think I should look for? Do you have a job? Can we meet next week to talk about it? Write soon, Sam

Notes: say what job Sam should look for and why. Tell Sam about a job you have or would like. Suggest when and where to meet.

Write your email to Sam in about 100 words.
items.sample: Hi Sam, Thanks for your email. It is a great idea to look for a job this summer! I think you should try working in a cafe or a shop near your home, because you like talking to people. I have a small job myself. I help my aunt in her flower shop on Saturdays, and I really enjoy it because I learn something new every week. She pays me ten dollars an hour, which is not a lot, but it is enough for my cinema tickets. Yes, I would love to meet next week to talk about it. How about Wednesday afternoon after school? We could go to the library and look at the job notices together. Tell me what time suits you. Write soon, Lin
items.vi: Trả lời email của Sam: gợi ý loại việc làm và lý do, kể về công việc của bạn, rồi hẹn thời gian địa điểm gặp (khoảng 100 từ).

parts.instr: Write a story.
parts.instrVi: Viết một câu chuyện.

items.q:
Your English teacher has asked you to write a story. Your story must begin with this sentence:

When the phone rang, Lisa could not believe the good news.

Write your story in about 100 words.
items.sample: When the phone rang, Lisa could not believe the good news. A woman from the City Museum said that Lisa had won the summer job she wanted so much. She jumped up and shouted, because she had waited for two weeks. Her mother ran into the room and asked what was wrong. Lisa was so happy that she could not speak for a moment. Then she explained everything. The next morning she wore her best dress and went to the museum by bus. Her new boss showed her the old maps and paintings, and Lisa learned how to take care of them. At the end of the day she was tired but very happy. She decided that she wanted to work with history for the rest of her life.
items.vi: Viết câu chuyện bắt đầu bằng câu cho sẵn: Lisa nhận được tin vui qua điện thoại (khoảng 100 từ).

parts.instr: Answer the examiner's questions about yourself.
parts.instrVi: Trả lời các câu hỏi của giám khảo về bản thân.

items.q: What is your favorite subject at school, and why?
items.sample: My favorite subject is English because I like learning new words, and my teacher makes the lessons fun.
items.vi: Nói môn học yêu thích và lý do.

items.q: What job would you like to do in the future?
items.sample: In the future I would like to be a doctor because I want to help people who are ill and to work in a hospital.
items.vi: Nói nghề bạn muốn làm trong tương lai và lý do.

items.q: Does anyone in your family have an interesting job?
items.sample: Yes, my mother works as a nurse. It is a hard job, but she says she loves helping her patients every day.
items.vi: Kể về công việc thú vị của người thân.

items.q: What do you usually do after school?
items.sample: After school I usually go home, have a snack and do my homework, and then I help my parents cook dinner.
items.vi: Nói bạn thường làm gì sau giờ học.

parts.instr: Describe the photo.
parts.instrVi: Miêu tả bức ảnh.

items.q: Look at the photo. Describe what the young cook is doing and say how you think she feels.
items.sample: In this photo I can see a young woman in a kitchen. She is wearing a white uniform and a tall hat, so I think she is a cook. She is cooking something in a big pan, and there are some vegetables on the table next to her. I think she is happy because she is smiling and she looks very busy. Maybe she works in a restaurant. I would not like to cook all day, but it looks like a very interesting job.
items.vi: Miêu tả bức ảnh: cô gái làm bếp đang nấu ăn, mặc gì, cảm thấy thế nào.

parts.instr: Talk about the situation and make a decision.
parts.instrVi: Thảo luận tình huống và đưa ra quyết định.

items.q: Your school is planning a Careers Day and wants to invite visitors. The choices are a chef, a vet, a firefighter, an engineer and a pilot. Talk together about which visitors would be most interesting, and decide which two to invite.
items.sample: I think the vet would be very interesting because many students love animals. The chef is a good idea too, because the students could taste some food. The firefighter would be exciting, but I think the visit might be short. The pilot could tell us about different countries, but it may be hard for a pilot to come on a weekday. So I would invite the vet and the chef. What do you think? I believe these two jobs are the most useful for students, because they are close to everyday life.
items.vi: Thảo luận và chọn hai khách mời cho ngày hướng nghiệp, nêu lý do cho từng lựa chọn.

parts.instr: Answer the question and give reasons.
parts.instrVi: Trả lời câu hỏi và nêu lý do.

items.q: Do you think it is better to have the same job for many years or to change jobs often? Why?
items.sample: In my opinion it is better to change jobs sometimes, because you can learn new things and meet new people. If you do the same job for many years, you may get bored. However, I understand that a steady job is safer, and it gives you more money when you have a family. So I think the best way is to stay in a job for a few years and then try something different. That is what my uncle did, and he is very happy now.
items.vi: Nêu ý kiến: nên giữ một công việc lâu năm hay đổi việc thường xuyên, kèm lý do.

parts.instr: For each question, choose the correct picture.
parts.instrVi: Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn bức tranh đúng.

audio.t: What did Mia's cousin bring to the party?
Did your cousin bring a cake to your party, Mia?
No, my aunt made the cake at home. My cousin brought a lot of balloons, and a present came from my uncle.

items.q: What did Mia's cousin bring to the party?
items.vi: Bánh do dì làm, quà từ chú, còn 'my cousin brought a lot of balloons' (anh/chị họ mang nhiều bóng bay).

audio.t: Where will Jack meet his friend?
Are you meeting Leo at school, Jack?
No, school is closed today. We are going to the pool after lunch, so I will meet him there.

items.q: Where will Jack meet his friend?
items.vi: Trường đóng cửa, hai bạn 'going to the pool' (đến hồ bơi), nên gặp nhau ở hồ bơi.

audio.t: What present did the girl buy for her grandmother?
Did you buy flowers for Grandma?
She has lots of flowers in her garden. I thought about a scarf, but she has too many. In the end I bought her a book of old stories.

items.q: What present did the girl buy for her grandmother?
items.vi: Bà đã có nhiều hoa và khăn, nên cô bé 'bought her a book' (mua một quyển sách).

audio.t: What is the boy's sister doing now?
Is your sister playing the piano?
No, she did that earlier. Now she's on the phone with her best friend. Later she will cook dinner.

items.q: What is the boy's sister doing now?
items.vi: Chị chơi piano lúc trước và sẽ nấu ăn sau; bây giờ chị 'on the phone' (đang nói chuyện điện thoại).

audio.t: What will the family eat for dinner on Sunday?
Shall we have pizza on Sunday?
We had pizza last week. Grandpa wants soup, and it will be cold.
Pasta, then?
No, soup is better.

items.q: What will the family eat for dinner on Sunday?
items.vi: Pizza ăn tuần trước, mì ống bị từ chối; cuối cùng 'soup is better' (súp thì tốt hơn).

audio.t: Which room did the girl clean?
Did you clean the kitchen today?
No, my brother did that. Mom did the bathroom. I cleaned my bedroom.

items.q: Which room did the girl clean?
items.vi: Anh trai dọn bếp, mẹ dọn phòng tắm, còn cô bé dọn 'my bedroom' (phòng ngủ của mình).

audio.t: What does the girl want for her birthday?
Do you want a new bike for your birthday?
I already have one. Dad says headphones are enough, but what I really want is a camera.

items.q: What does the girl want for her birthday?
items.vi: Cô bé đã có xe đạp, bố nói tai nghe là đủ, nhưng điều cô thật sự muốn là 'a camera' (máy ảnh).

parts.instr: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.instrVi: Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn đáp án đúng.

audio.t: Why is the girl upset?
You look sad, Anna. What's wrong?
My best friend Kate is moving to another city next month.
I'm sorry. Can you visit her?
Maybe in the holidays.

items.q: Why is the girl upset?
options: She had a fight with her sister.
items.vi: Anna buồn vì 'Kate is moving to another city' (Kate sắp chuyển đến thành phố khác).

audio.t: What does the man think about the family trip?
I think a weekend at the lake is a good idea.
Isn't it too cold?
Not in July. And the children will love swimming there.

items.q: What does the man think about the family trip?
options: It will be fun for the children.
items.vi: Người đàn ông nói tháng Bảy không lạnh và 'the children will love swimming' (bọn trẻ sẽ thích bơi), nên chuyến đi vui cho trẻ.

audio.t: What will they give their dad?
Shall we get Dad a shirt for his birthday?
He has so many shirts. How about a cooking class?
Great idea! He loves cooking.

items.q: What will they give their dad?
items.vi: Họ bỏ ý tưởng áo sơ mi vì bố có nhiều rồi; cả hai đồng ý tặng 'a cooking class' (một lớp nấu ăn).

audio.t: How does the boy feel about his new school?
How is your new school, Sam?
It's better than I expected. I've made two friends already. The homework is hard, but I don't mind.

items.q: How does the boy feel about his new school?
options: He is afraid of the teachers.
items.vi: Sam nói trường 'better than I expected' (tốt hơn mong đợi) và đã có hai bạn, nên cậu hài lòng.

audio.t: What does the woman want Tim to do?
Tim, please turn off the TV and help me with dinner.
Can I finish this show first?
It's late. Please set the table now.

items.q: What does the woman want Tim to do?
items.vi: Mẹ bảo Tim tắt TV và 'set the table now' (dọn bàn ăn ngay).

audio.t: Why can't the girl come to the party on Saturday?
Can you come to Joe's party on Saturday?
I'd love to, but we are visiting my grandparents. They live three hours away.

items.q: Why can't the girl come to the party on Saturday?
options: She is going to see relatives.
items.vi: Cô bé phải 'visiting my grandparents' (đi thăm ông bà), tức là đi thăm họ hàng.

parts.instr: You will hear a woman talking about a family day. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.instrVi: Bạn sẽ nghe một người phụ nữ nói về một ngày hội gia đình. Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn đáp án đúng.

audio.t: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Friends and Family Day at Greenfield Park. My name is Laura and I'm the organizer.
First, the weather. It will be sunny until lunchtime, but rain is possible in the afternoon, so please keep your umbrellas with you.
We start at ten o'clock with a game of football. Teams are made of both adults and children, so grandparents are very welcome to play!
If you prefer something quieter, there is a painting table next to the lake where you can paint a picture of your family.
At twelve thirty we will have lunch. Please bring your own sandwiches, because the cafe is closed this year, but we will give everyone a free drink.
After lunch there is a talent show. If you want to take part, please tell Mr. Evans before eleven o'clock. The prize this year is a picnic basket.
Finally, parking. The big car park is full, so please use the small one behind the school and walk five minutes to the park. Thank you, and enjoy the day.

items.q: What does Laura say about the weather?
options: It may rain later in the day.
It will be sunny all day.
It will be cold in the morning.
items.vi: Laura nói trời nắng đến trưa nhưng 'rain is possible in the afternoon' (chiều có thể mưa).

items.q: Who can play in the football teams?
items.vi: 'Teams are made of both adults and children' (đội gồm cả người lớn và trẻ em).

items.q: What can people do by the lake?
items.vi: Bên hồ có 'a painting table' (bàn vẽ) để vẽ tranh gia đình.

items.q: What should people do about lunch?
items.vi: Quán cà phê đóng cửa nên 'bring your own sandwiches' (tự mang bánh mì kẹp).

items.q: Who should people tell if they want to join the talent show?
items.vi: Ai muốn tham gia phải báo cho 'Mr. Evans' trước 11 giờ.

items.q: Where should drivers park?
items.vi: Bãi lớn đã đầy, nên dùng bãi nhỏ 'behind the school' (phía sau trường).

parts.instr: You will hear an interview with a woman who has written a book about friendship. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.instrVi: Bạn sẽ nghe một cuộc phỏng vấn với một người phụ nữ đã viết sách về tình bạn. Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn đáp án đúng.

audio.t: Today I'm talking to Dr. Helen Park, who has written a book about teenage friendship. Welcome, Helen.
Thank you.
Helen, why did you write the book?
Well, when my daughter started at a new school, she lost touch with her old friends and felt very lonely. I wanted to help families understand how hard that can be.
What is your first piece of advice for teenagers?
Join a club. It's easier to talk to people when you share an interest, like chess or drawing, than to start a conversation in the hallway.
And if a teenager is shy?
Start small. Say hello to one new person each day. Friendships grow slowly, and two close friends are better than twenty people who hardly know you.
Many parents worry about their children's friends. What should they do?
Invite them for dinner. When parents get to know the friends, they usually worry much less, and the teenagers feel respected.
What about arguments between friends?
They are normal. Wait until you are calm, then listen to the other person without interrupting. Saying sorry early is a good idea, too.
Finally, are you planning another book?
Yes, it will be about brothers and sisters. I find the subject fascinating, and my two sons argue every day!
We'll look forward to reading it. Thank you, Helen.

items.q: Why did Helen write the book?
options: She used to be a school teacher.
Her daughter felt lonely at a new school.
Her friends asked her to write it.
items.vi: Con gái bà chuyển trường, mất liên lạc bạn cũ và 'felt very lonely' (cảm thấy rất cô đơn).

items.q: What is her first piece of advice?
items.vi: Lời khuyên đầu tiên là 'Join a club' (tham gia câu lạc bộ) để có sở thích chung.

items.q: What does she say shy teenagers should do?
options: Try to have lots of friends
Say hello to one new person each day
Wait for others to speak first
items.vi: Bà khuyên 'Say hello to one new person each day' (mỗi ngày chào một người mới).

items.q: What should parents do about their children's friends?
items.vi: Cha mẹ nên 'Invite them for dinner' (mời các bạn ăn tối) để hiểu họ hơn.

items.q: What does Helen say about arguments?
options: They mean the friendship is over.
They are best forgotten at once.
They should be solved when people are calm.
items.vi: Bà nói hãy 'wait until you are calm' (đợi đến khi bình tĩnh) rồi lắng nghe người kia.

items.q: What will her next book be about?
items.vi: Cuốn sách tiếp theo nói về 'brothers and sisters' (anh chị em).

parts.instr: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.instrVi: Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn đáp án đúng.

items.text: Hi Dan, I'm at Grandma's until six. Your dinner is in the fridge. Just heat it for two minutes. Love, Mom
items.q: What should Dan do?
items.vi: Mẹ để sẵn bữa tối trong tủ lạnh và bảo 'heat it for two minutes' (hâm nóng hai phút).

items.text: FAMILY SWIMMING HOUR. Saturdays, 4 to 5 p.m. Children under ten must come with an adult. Tickets: $2 each.
items.q: What does the notice say?
options: Young children must have an adult with them.
Only families can swim on Saturdays.
items.vi: Thông báo nói trẻ dưới mười tuổi 'must come with an adult' (phải đi cùng người lớn).

items.text: Dear Mr. and Mrs. Lopez, Today your son Carlos was very kind to a new student and helped her find her classroom. We are very proud of him. Mrs. Reed
items.q: Why did Mrs. Reed write?
options: To ask for help with a school trip
To say something good about Carlos
items.vi: Cô Reed viết để khen Carlos vì đã giúp một học sinh mới, tức là nói điều tốt về em.

items.text: Sara, can we change our plans for Friday? My cousin is visiting, so I can't go shopping with you. Are you free on Saturday instead? Kim
items.q: What does Kim want to do?
options: Go shopping on a different day
items.vi: Kim hỏi Sara có rảnh 'on Saturday instead' (thay vào đó vào thứ Bảy) không, tức là đổi ngày đi mua sắm.

items.text: QUIET, PLEASE. Mrs. Gray's baby goes to sleep at nine p.m. Thank you, your neighbors.
items.q: What does the sign ask people to do?
options: Visit Mrs. Gray in the evening
items.vi: Biển báo yêu cầu giữ yên lặng vì em bé ngủ lúc chín giờ tối.

parts.instr: Read about three places for family weekends. For each question, choose the correct place.
parts.instrVi: Đọc về ba địa điểm cho cuối tuần gia đình. Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn địa điểm đúng.

items.text:
Three places for family weekends

Oakwood Farm: Families can feed the animals and pick fruit in the garden. There is a small cafe where you can have lunch, and children under five can play in a safe sand area. Open Saturdays and Sundays, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Dogs are not allowed.

Craft Corner: This workshop is for parents and children who like making things. Every Sunday afternoon you can learn to make pots, cards or small bags. All the materials are included in the price, and there is a quiet room where parents can read while teenagers work on their own projects.

Riverside Games Club: A friendly club in the old library where families play board games together on Friday evenings. Beginners get a free lesson at six o'clock. Snacks are on sale, and groups of five or more people get a ten percent discount.

items.q: The Wilson family has a three-year-old child and wants a safe place outdoors.
items.vi: Trẻ ba tuổi cần chỗ an toàn: Oakwood Farm có 'safe sand area' (khu cát an toàn) cho trẻ dưới năm tuổi.

items.q: Mei wants to read quietly while her teenage son makes things.
items.vi: Craft Corner có 'a quiet room where parents can read' (phòng yên tĩnh để cha mẹ đọc sách).

items.q: Six cousins want to meet on a Friday evening and pay less.
items.vi: Riverside mở tối thứ Sáu và nhóm từ năm người được 'ten percent discount' (giảm 10%).

items.q: Mr. Adams wants to make a gift for his mother without buying extra things.
items.vi: Ở Craft Corner 'all the materials are included' (đã gồm mọi nguyên liệu), nên không phải mua thêm.

items.q: The Brown family wants to have a meal after a Saturday morning visit.
items.vi: Chỉ Oakwood Farm mở thứ Bảy và có quán cà phê 'where you can have lunch' (ăn trưa).

parts.instr: Read the article. For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.instrVi: Đọc bài báo. Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn đáp án đúng.

items.text:
Growing up with my cousin Leo
by Nina Ortega

When people ask me who my best friend is, I always say the same thing: my cousin Leo. We are the same age, and since we were babies our mothers have taken us everywhere together. Some people think it is strange to be best friends with a relative, but for me it feels completely natural.

Leo lives in a different town, about two hours away by train, so we only see each other during the holidays and on some weekends. When I was younger, I hated the long gaps between visits. I used to write him letters, which he answered with drawings because he said his handwriting was terrible. I still have a box full of them under my bed.

Last summer we had our first real argument. I had planned to spend the week at the beach, but Leo wanted to stay at his grandparents' farm and help his grandfather with the apples. I thought that sounded boring and told him so. He didn't speak to me for a whole day. In the end my aunt sat us down and asked each of us to explain how we felt. It turned out that Leo had not seen his grandfather for months and was worried about him. I felt terrible. We went to the farm together, and to my surprise I enjoyed picking apples much more than lying on the sand.

That week taught me something important. Friends do not always have to like the same things, but they should listen to each other. With Leo, it is easy because we have known each other for so long. With my school friends, I am still learning. Last month, a classmate told me she was sad because she had to move house, and instead of changing the subject, I asked her questions and let her talk. She said it was the nicest thing anyone had done for her that week.

Next year Leo's family is moving to my town, and I can hardly wait. People ask me whether we will get tired of each other. I don't think so. Even if we do argue again, I know we will find a way to make up, just as we did on the farm.

items.q: What is Nina's opinion about being best friends with a relative?
options: It is difficult when you live far apart.
items.vi: Nina nói với cô việc đó 'feels completely natural' (hoàn toàn tự nhiên), dù người khác thấy lạ.

items.q: Why did Leo answer Nina's letters with drawings?
options: He thought his writing was bad.
He wanted her to draw, too.
items.vi: Leo nói 'his handwriting was terrible' (chữ viết của cậu rất xấu) nên trả lời bằng tranh vẽ.

items.q: What caused the argument last summer?
options: Leo was rude to his grandfather.
Nina lost something that belonged to Leo.
They wanted to spend the week in different places.
items.vi: Nina muốn ra biển còn Leo muốn ở lại nông trại, nên hai bạn muốn đi những nơi khác nhau.

items.q: What did Nina learn from the argument?
options: Relatives are better than school friends.
Friends should listen to each other.
items.vi: Cô học được rằng bạn bè 'should listen to each other' (nên lắng nghe nhau), dù không thích giống nhau.

items.q: Why does Nina mention her classmate?
options: To explain why she is moving
To show that she now listens better to friends
items.vi: Nina kể chuyện bạn cùng lớp để cho thấy cô đã biết lắng nghe, hỏi han thay vì đổi chủ đề.

parts.instr: Five sentences have been removed from the paragraphs. Choose the correct sentence for each gap.
parts.instrVi: Năm câu đã bị lược khỏi các đoạn văn. Chọn câu đúng cho mỗi chỗ trống.

items.text: My grandmother lives alone in a small flat near the market. ＿ Every Saturday I help her carry her bags home, and we have tea together.
items.q: Choose the sentence that fits the gap.
options: She moved there when she was a student.
She likes watching television in the evening.
She has two sisters in another country.
She loves going shopping for fresh vegetables.
items.vi: Câu sau nói 'help her carry her bags' (giúp bà xách túi), nên câu thiếu phải nói bà thích đi mua rau.

items.text: Tom and his brother share a bedroom, and they often argue about the mess. ＿ Last week their father put a line of tape on the floor, and now each boy keeps his half tidy.
items.q: Choose the sentence that fits the gap.
options: Tom has a big collection of old coins.
The room is on the second floor of the house.
Their cousins sometimes sleep in the room, too.
Finally, their parents got tired of the noise.
items.vi: Câu sau kể người cha dán băng keo để giải quyết, nên câu trước cần nói cha mẹ đã chán cảnh ồn ào.

items.text: Maya met her best friend, Zoe, on the first day of primary school. ＿ They have been inseparable ever since.
items.q: Choose the sentence that fits the gap.
options: Zoe lives in a house with a red door.
They both want to be doctors one day.
Maya's mother works in a hospital.
The teacher put them at the same desk, and they began to talk.
items.vi: Câu cần giải thích hai bạn quen nhau thế nào: cô giáo xếp ngồi cùng bàn rồi họ bắt đầu nói chuyện.

items.text: Ali's family always eats dinner together at seven o'clock. ＿ That is why Ali says dinner is his favorite part of the day.
items.q: Choose the sentence that fits the gap.
options: The kitchen has a big wooden table.
His sister finishes her homework before dinner.
His father usually cooks pasta with tomatoes.

audio.t: Today I'm talking to Mara Jensen, who sells bread at food festivals. Mara, why did you start?

Is the baking the hardest part?

Which bread sells best?

Start small. Don't buy expensive equipment at the beginning, and always taste your food before you sell it.

Harbor Seafood Weekend
This festival is held on the old pier every June. Visitors can watch chefs cook fish on big grills and try small portions for $2 each. There are no seats, so most people eat standing up. Children can play a free fishing game. For safety, dogs are not allowed on the pier. Open 10 am to 6 pm.

This is held in the streets of the old town in November. More than fifty stalls sell spices, tea and sweets from many countries. Cooks give a ten-minute show every hour. Entry is free and dogs are welcome. Most stalls are outdoors, so wear warm clothes. Open noon to 8 pm.

items.text:
Every year, on the last Saturday before the New Year, my whole family comes to our house for Dumpling Night. It is the loudest, messiest and happiest evening of my year, and I would not change it for anything.

The work starts at four o'clock. My grandfather mixes the dough in a huge bowl, because he says nobody else knows how soft it should be. My aunts chop cabbage and pork for the filling, while the younger cousins roll the dough into little circles. Then comes the difficult part: closing each dumpling so that it does not open in the water. The first time I tried, mine looked like small, sad hats and fell apart in the pot. Everyone laughed, and I wanted to hide under the table. But my grandfather just smiled and said, "Every great cook starts with a bad dumpling." After that, I felt much better.

There is also a secret in the kitchen. Before we start, Grandpa puts a clean coin into one dumpling, and he never tells us which one. Whoever finds it is supposed to have good luck for the whole year. Last year my cousin Theo found it, and he was so pleased that he did not stop talking for an hour. I secretly think Theo cheated, because he bit into every dumpling very carefully.

What I enjoy most, though, is not the eating. While our hands are busy, each person has to tell one story about the past year. Some are funny, some are a little sad, and a few make my aunts cry with laughter. I learn things about my family that I never knew, like the fact that my dad once got lost in the market for two hours.

By nine o'clock the table is covered in flour and everybody is tired but happy. Next year, I would like to invite my best friend, Maria, so she can try our tradition. I hope she is better at closing dumplings than I was.

To explain how to cook a meal
To complain about a messy evening

items.vi: Cô thầm nghĩ Theo gian lận vì cậu cắn từng chiếc sủi cảo rất cẩn thận.

items.q: What does Nora like best about Dumpling Night?
items.vi: Điều cô thích nhất không phải ăn mà là kể và nghe chuyện trong lúc làm.

items.q: What does Nora hope to do next year?
items.vi: Năm sau cô muốn mời bạn thân Maria đến thử truyền thống này.

parts.instr: Five sentences have been removed from the paragraphs. For each question, choose the correct sentence.
parts.instrVi: Mỗi đoạn văn bị bỏ một câu. Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn câu đúng.

items.text: Last weekend our class held a pancake breakfast at school. We started cooking at seven. ＿ By eight o'clock, the first parents were already waiting outside the hall. Soon every table was full, and we hardly had time to sit down.
items.q: Which sentence fits the gap?
options: The school was closed for the holidays.
I never eat breakfast on Sundays.
Pancakes are usually made with eggs, milk and flour.
The smell of hot pancakes soon filled the whole building.
items.vi: Câu cần điền giải thích vì sao phụ huynh đã đứng chờ lúc 8 giờ: mùi bánh crepe thơm khắp tòa nhà.

items.text: Maya's grandmother makes a special soup every winter festival. ＿ Maya has watched her for years, but she can never copy the taste. Last year she asked for the recipe, and her grandmother only smiled.
items.q: Which sentence fits the gap?
options: The soup is served in small blue bowls at school.
Everyone in the family prefers rice to soup.
Maya's grandmother lives in a very big city.
She never uses a book or a scale, and she adds things by feel.
items.vi: Câu sau nói Maya không thể bắt chước được vị, nên câu cần điền là bà không dùng sách hay cân mà nêm theo cảm giác.

items.text: Our town's lantern parade starts at sunset. Hundreds of children walk down Main Street with paper lanterns. ＿ After the parade, everyone goes to the square for hot chocolate and cake.
items.q: Which sentence fits the gap?
options: The town has a new library.
The shops on Main Street open at nine in the morning.
Hot chocolate is too sweet for some people.
Some lanterns are shaped like fish, birds and even rockets, and they are made at school.
items.vi: Câu cần điền nói thêm về những chiếc đèn lồng mà trẻ em cầm trong đoàn diễu hành.

items.text: Dan wanted to surprise his mother on her birthday. He got up early and went to the kitchen. ＿ When she came downstairs, the table was ready and there was a card next to her cup.
items.q: Which sentence fits the gap?
options: His mother works at a bank in the city.
The shops were closed because of snow.
Dan's brother plays soccer on Saturdays.
He made scrambled eggs and toast, and he even cut up some fruit.
items.vi: Khi mẹ xuống nhà bàn đã sẵn sàng, nên Dan đã làm bữa sáng trong bếp.

items.text: Every August, our village has a tomato festival. Farmers bring baskets of tomatoes of every color to the market. ＿ In the afternoon, there is a contest to find the heaviest tomato, and last year's winner weighed over two pounds.
items.q: Which sentence fits the gap?
options: Most people in the village prefer to eat apples.
Winter in the village is long and cold.
The farmers go to bed very early every night.
Visitors can taste soups, salads and sauces made from them.
items.vi: Câu cần điền nói về các món làm từ cà chua mà khách có thể nếm tại lễ hội.

parts.instr: For each question, choose the correct word.
parts.instrVi: Mỗi câu hỏi, chọn từ đúng.

items.text: We need to ＿ a table at the restaurant for Saturday because it is always full.
items.q: Choose the correct word.
items.vi: Book a table = đặt bàn trước vì nhà hàng luôn kín chỗ.

items.text: The soup was so ＿ that I couldn't finish it.
items.q: Choose the correct word.
items.vi: Salty = mặn; súp quá mặn nên không ăn hết được.

items.text: She was so ＿ about the festival that she woke up at five to get ready.
items.q: Choose the correct word.
items.vi: Excited = háo hức; quá háo hức về lễ hội nên dậy lúc 5 giờ.

items.text: My uncle is a ＿ . He cooks in a big hotel.
items.q: Choose the correct word.
items.vi: Chef = đầu bếp, người nấu ăn trong khách sạn lớn.

items.text: Grandma gave me her ＿ for chocolate cake, with a list of everything I need.
items.q: Choose the correct word.
items.vi: Recipe = công thức nấu ăn, có danh sách nguyên liệu.

parts.instr: For each question, write ONE word in the gap.
parts.instrVi: Mỗi câu hỏi, điền MỘT từ vào chỗ trống.

items.text: We always have a big dinner ＿ New Year's Eve.
items.vi: on + ngày cụ thể: on New Year's Eve (vào đêm giao thừa).

items.text: My sister is very good ＿ cooking noodles.
items.vi: be good at + V-ing: giỏi làm gì.

items.text: How ＿ sugar do you put in your tea?
items.vi: sugar không đếm được nên dùng How much.

items.text: If it ＿ tomorrow, the picnic will be moved indoors.
items.vi: Câu điều kiện loại 1: if + hiện tại đơn (it rains).

items.text: This beautiful cake was made ＿ my grandmother.
items.vi: Câu bị động: made by + người làm ra.
